42cursus-42sh.name: 42sh
42cursus-42sh.description: This project consists of creating a complete shell. A minimum set of functionalities is asked, from which you will build your own finalized shell, potentially going as far as job control and shell scripting. This project will involve a large variety of standard UNIX (and POSIX) functionalities.
42cursus-42sh.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/215874/en.subject.pdf

bgp-at-doors-of-autonomous-systems-is-si.name: Bgp At Doors of Autonomous Systems is Simple
bgp-at-doors-of-autonomous-systems-is-si.description:
The purpose of this project is to deepen your knowledge of NetPractice.
 You will have to simulate several networks (VXLAN+BGP-EVPN) in GNS3.
bgp-at-doors-of-autonomous-systems-is-si.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211017/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-doom-nukem.name: doom-nukem
42cursus-doom-nukem.description: Doom Nukem pushes the possibilities of Raycasting much further while bringing a dimension of Game design, so you are going to have to make a mix of Doom and Duke Nukem 3D.  It's up to you to find the one that suits you and that will allow you to add the requested features as well as those you want to see there.
42cursus-doom-nukem.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210723/en.subject.pdf

inception-of-things.name: Inception-of-Things
inception-of-things.description:
This project aims to introduce you to Kubernetes from a developer's perspective.
 You will have to set up small clusters and discover the mechanics of continuous integration.
 At the end of this project, you will be able to set up a working cluster in Docker and have a usable continuous integration pipeline for your applications.
inception-of-things.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/224141/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-humangl.name: humangl
42cursus-humangl.description: This intermediate OpenGL project is an introduction to hierarchical modeling. You will learn to use matrices in order to link various parts of a humanoid model, and animate them.
42cursus-humangl.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/217474/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-2.name: kfs-2
42cursus-kfs-2.description: Discover the world of Kernel Programming and learn how to create your very own Kernel from scratch.
42cursus-kfs-2.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208608/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-override.name: override
42cursus-override.description: Override is the direct sequel to Rainfall, and it is another level entirely. Rainfall taught you the stack; Override drops you into modern, fully mitigated 64-bit binaries on glibc 2.39, all protections on by default. Stripped binaries, no shortcuts, the heap and the network in play. This is serious binary exploitation. Come prepared.
42cursus-override.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221873/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-pestilence.name: pestilence
42cursus-pestilence.description: Second virus project. Reuse the Famine base to add a hiding method of your code.
42cursus-pestilence.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208626/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-rt.name: rt
42cursus-rt.description: RT pushes the limits of what Ray Tracing can do: mirror effect, transparency, object cutting, texture application... . Use the preceding project to create an infrastructure capable of supporting all these ramifications and obtain sublime computer-generated images.
42cursus-rt.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210513/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-total-perspective-vortex.name: total-perspective-vortex
42cursus-total-perspective-vortex.description: Learn to use python tools to process large dimension data, and create a man-machine interface thanks to brainwaves.
42cursus-total-perspective-vortex.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209510/en.subject.pdf

piscine-symfony.name: Piscine Symfony
piscine-symfony.description: Piscines are an important time in your cursus, during which you will have the occasion to learn a new language, or even a new paradigm!
piscine-symfony.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209481/en.subject.pdf

piscine-django.name: Piscine Django
piscine-django.description: Piscines are an important time in your cursus, during which you will have the occasion to learn a new language, or even a new paradigm!
piscine-django.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210657/en.subject.pdf

piscine-ror.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210088/en.subject.pdf

mobile.description: Piscines are an important time in your cursus, during which you will have the occasion to learn a new language, or even a new paradigm!
mobile.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/212922/en.subject.pdf

piscine-object.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210719/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-piscine-ocaml.name: Piscine ocaml
42cursus-piscine-ocaml.description: Piscines are an important time in your cursus, during which you will have the occasion to learn a new language, or even a new paradigm!
42cursus-piscine-ocaml.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208548/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-camagru.name: camagru
42cursus-camagru.description: This project is a warm-up for web development. You will need to create a small, Instagram-like website that allows users to create and share photomontages. From scratch, you will implement the basic functionalities commonly used by any website with a user base.
42cursus-camagru.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/203658/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-matcha.name: matcha
42cursus-matcha.description: This second project introduces a more advanced tool for building web applications: the micro-framework. You are invited to create a dating site in the programming language of your choice. User interaction is at the heart of this project!
42cursus-matcha.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/227569/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-hypertube.name: hypertube
42cursus-hypertube.description: Hypertube introduces you to a powerful category of tools: MVC frameworks. You will learn how to work with an MVC framework—using the programming language of your choice—to build a video streaming website with content downloaded via the BitTorrent protocol.
42cursus-hypertube.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209673/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-red-tetris.name: red-tetris
42cursus-red-tetris.description: The objective of this project is to develop a networked multiplayer Tetris game using a software stack that is exclusively Full Stack JavaScript.
42cursus-red-tetris.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211093/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-darkly.name: darkly
42cursus-darkly.description: Introductory project to computer security in the specific field of the web, this project has you audit a deliberately vulnerable web platform. You will exploit real-world vulnerabilities to escalate your access from an anonymous visitor all the way up to administrator, capture the flags hidden along the way, and understand how each breach could have been prevented, both from a programming and a design perspective.
42cursus-darkly.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221875/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-h42n42.name: h42n42
42cursus-h42n42.description: An introductory project to the OCSIGEN framework for creating rich web applications in OCaml. The goal is to design a simulator where creatures try to escape a dangerous virus.
42cursus-h42n42.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209576/en.subject.pdf

tokenizer.name: Tokenizer
tokenizer.description: This project allows you to learn the basics in web3. You will have to create your personal token!
tokenizer.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211049/en.subject.pdf

tokenizeart.name: TokenizeArt
tokenizeart.description: This project allows you to learn the basics in web3. You will have to create your non-fungible token!
tokenizeart.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/214858/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-music-room.name: music-room
42cursus-music-room.description: In a group, create a complete mobile app for collaborative playlists using a relevant SDK and API. The tasks include mobile development, back-end development, and the creation of a REST API.
42cursus-music-room.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209570/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_hangouts.name: ft_hangouts
42cursus-ft_hangouts.description: The goal of this project is to introduce you to mobile application development. You will build a contact management app for Android, allowing users to create, manage, and interact with their contacts. Throughout the project, you will learn how a mobile app works, how the Android system manages application lifecycles, and how to use the Android SDK effectively.
42cursus-ft_hangouts.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208715/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-swifty-companion.name: swifty-companion
42cursus-swifty-companion.description: This project is an introduction to mobile programming. The goal is to create, an application which will allow you to get infos about 42students, using the API.
42cursus-swifty-companion.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211725/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-swifty-proteins.name: swifty-proteins
42cursus-swifty-proteins.description:
Build a professional mobile application for visualizing protein ligands in 3D. 
You'll fetch molecular data from the RCSB Protein Data Bank, parse Chemical Information 
Files (.cif format), and render complex molecular structures using native 3D frameworks 
(SceneKit on iOS or equivalent on Android). The app features secure biometric authentication, 
interactive 3D models with CPK coloring and ball-and-stick representation, gesture-based 
controls for rotation and zoom, and social sharing capabilities. This project combines 
bioinformatics, mobile security, network programming, and advanced 3D graphics rendering.
42cursus-swifty-proteins.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/216248/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-bomberman.name: bomberman
42cursus-bomberman.description: Bomberman is a classic video game: as simple in its gameplay as it is fun to play! You will leverage its simplicity here to undertake your first major professional-grade C++ project. Your goal is to recode a version of Bomberman in C++ and OpenGL, with the aim of creating the most polished game possible.
42cursus-bomberman.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209477/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-nibbler.name: nibbler
42cursus-nibbler.description: This project in C++ will make you recode a Snake where you can switch the interface at run time
42cursus-nibbler.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209541/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-avaj-launcher.name: avaj-launcher
42cursus-avaj-launcher.description: First project of the Java projects arc. Implementation of a simple Java program according to a given class diagram written in UML.
42cursus-avaj-launcher.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/217430/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-swingy.name: swingy
42cursus-swingy.description: This is the second project from the Java world at 42. You will learn to develop GUI applications with the SWING framework, in order to create an RPG game.
42cursus-swingy.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208601/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-fix-me.name: fix-me
42cursus-fix-me.description: Final project of the Java Programming arc. You will write a program that simulates stock exchanges and handles trading algorithms, including networking and socket implementations.
42cursus-fix-me.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208928/en.subject.pdf

libftpp.name: libftpp
libftpp.description: This subject aims to introduce you to advanced C++ concepts through the development of complex tools and systems.
libftpp.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/225598/en.subject.pdf

abstract_data.name: Abstract_data
abstract_data.description: The multiple available containers in C++ all have a very different usage. To make sure you understand them all, let's re-implement them!
abstract_data.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/225597/en.subject.pdf

retroemu.name: RetroEmu
retroemu.description: This project involves coding an emulator for an 8-bit handheld console (DMG model) and its color variant (CGB model). You will become familiar with technical documentation, better apprehend hardware emulation and understand the inner workings of a real piece of hardware as well as ROM cartridges.
retroemu.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/228207/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_turing.name: ft_turing
42cursus-ft_turing.description: ft_turing will help you discover the turing model using imperative programming through an implementation of this model with OCaml
42cursus-ft_turing.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209599/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_ality.name: ft_ality
42cursus-ft_ality.description: This project will get you acquainted with problems linked to automatic syntax analysis (“parsin”) by studying finite automation in a combat game.
42cursus-ft_ality.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210927/en.subject.pdf

libasm.name: libasm
libasm.description: The aim of this project is to become familiar with assembly language.
libasm.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/216943/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-zappy.name: zappy
42cursus-zappy.description: You will now create a multi-player game in a TCP/IP network. The game will consist of a server managing the game field, a graphic client which displays the state of the board, and IA clients that connect to the server to pilot a player on the filed. This is a real complete project that will let you express your creativity on top of your technical knowledge.
42cursus-zappy.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209870/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_linux.name: ft_linux
42cursus-ft_linux.description: The first project of the Kernel branch! This is a simple LFS so that you can build your own distribution which will be used in the next projects
42cursus-ft_linux.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/212191/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-little-penguin-1.name: little-penguin-1
42cursus-little-penguin-1.description: The start of a series of challenges inspired by Eudyptula. You will get acquainted with many points of Kernel development.
42cursus-little-penguin-1.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/217550/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-taskmaster.name: taskmaster
42cursus-taskmaster.description: This program is a job control task, in any language. The project is very close to the supervisor program on your computer
42cursus-taskmaster.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210912/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-strace.name: strace
42cursus-strace.description: First step in a serie of projects in C language leading to creation of a mini-GDB, this project will ask you to recode strace, a tool allowing you to list syscalls done by a running program
42cursus-strace.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209528/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-malloc.name: malloc
42cursus-malloc.description: What’s the deal with malloc? You’ve been using it since the piscine C but it’s not a system call. Find out the workings behind optimum memory management and recode it, as well as free and realloc.
42cursus-malloc.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/214587/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-matt-daemon.name: matt-daemon
42cursus-matt-daemon.description: A Unix project to create a server-type daemon. This server will listen on a given port and interpret a list of commands.
42cursus-matt-daemon.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/212499/en.subject.pdf

nm.name: nm
nm.description: This project will educate you on a deeper comprehension of how linux handle executables, by re-creating the command nm
nm.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221637/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-lem-ipc.name: lem-ipc
42cursus-lem-ipc.description: You have already learned how processes can communicate over a network using TCP/IP. Next, you will explore Unix tools that enable processes to communicate locally. You will practice these concepts by building a client for a classic board game.
42cursus-lem-ipc.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210295/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-1.name: kfs-1
42cursus-kfs-1.description: Discover the world of "Kernel Programming" and learn how to create your very own Kernel from scratch.
42cursus-kfs-1.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209026/en.subject.pdf

ft_malcolm.name: ft_malcolm
ft_malcolm.description: An introduction to network security with Man In The Middle attack
ft_malcolm.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/228824/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_ssl_md5.name: ft_ssl_md5
42cursus-ft_ssl_md5.description: You will recode part of the OpenSSL program, specifically the MD5 Hashing Algorithm.
42cursus-ft_ssl_md5.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/205815/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-snow-crash.name: snow-crash
42cursus-snow-crash.description: Eleven independent security challenges on a deliberately vulnerable Linux VM. Each level requires a distinct technique: binary analysis, process and filesystem inspection, code injection through configuration files and templates, protocol reverse engineering, jail escapes, and side-channel attacks. You will learn to read and exploit systems you did not write, using the tools and mindset of a security researcher.
42cursus-snow-crash.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221871/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-rainfall.name: rainfall
42cursus-rainfall.description: Rainfall picks up where Snow Crash left off and goes deeper. On a deliberately vulnerable VM, you climb from one account to the next by exploiting a series of SUID ELF binaries: reading their code, mapping how they lay out memory, and turning their flaws into control of execution. Each level tightens the protections (NX, stack canaries and ASLR), so your techniques must grow with them. Full RELRO and PIE await in the bonus part. Will you reach the last level?
42cursus-rainfall.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221872/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-boot2root.name: boot2root
42cursus-boot2root.description: This project introduces computer security through a hands-on challenge: you are given access to a deliberately vulnerable Linux server and must become root by at least two distinct methods. Each path requires reconnaissance, web exploitation, and a chain of privilege escalations across multiple user accounts. You will document every step in a writeup, explain the vulnerability behind each breach, and understand how it could have been prevented.
42cursus-boot2root.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221874/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_shield.name: ft_shield
42cursus-ft_shield.description: Use your skills to create a daemon to create your first basic trojan.
42cursus-ft_shield.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209357/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-woody-woodpacker.name: woody-woodpacker
42cursus-woody-woodpacker.description: A logical follow-up project on nm/otools that is designed to modify the headers of a ELF64 file. The goal here is to add a chunk of code and hide a non-stripped part of a file.
42cursus-woody-woodpacker.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/206044/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-famine.name: famine
42cursus-famine.description: Welcome to the wonderful world of viruses, trojans and other <Insert random antiVirus software>… Your goal here is to put your skills on handling binary files and make your first virus. WARNING: this project is solely for educational purposes!
42cursus-famine.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/212052/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_select.name: ft_select
42cursus-ft_select.description: The goal of this project is to get you started on terminal manipulation with termcaps. Here you will learn how to create a user interface for a program launched on the terminal.
42cursus-ft_select.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208555/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_script.name: ft_script
42cursus-ft_script.description: By re-coding the script command you will have the opportunity to understand interactions between user input and tty, notably line discipline as well as pseudo-terminals. Once the project finished, you will know why a Ctrl-C in your shell interrupts the ongoing program!
42cursus-ft_script.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/215689/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-cloud-1.name: cloud-1
42cursus-cloud-1.description: This project is an introduction to cloud servers.
42cursus-cloud-1.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208938/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-drivers-and-interrupts.name: drivers-and-interrupts
42cursus-drivers-and-interrupts.description: Learn how to connect a driver to your kernel. We will use a keyboard driver for this project.
42cursus-drivers-and-interrupts.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208587/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-dslr.name: dslr
42cursus-dslr.description: Discover Data Science through this project by recreating the Hogwarts Sorting Hat using logistic regression!
42cursus-dslr.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211419/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-expert-system.name: expert-system
42cursus-expert-system.description: This project involves creating, in the language of your choice, an expert system in proposal calculation. In other words, a program that can reason on a set of rules and initial facts to deduce other facts.
42cursus-expert-system.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210325/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-filesystem.name: filesystem
42cursus-filesystem.description: Create your own filesystem, for your linux kernel.
42cursus-filesystem.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208599/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_linear_regression.name: ft_linear_regression
42cursus-ft_linear_regression.description: This project will be your first steps into AI and Machine Learning. You're going to start with a simple, basic machine learning algorithm. You will have to create a program that predicts the price of a car by using a linear function train with a gradient descent algorithm.
42cursus-ft_linear_regression.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/212344/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_nmap.name: ft_nmap
42cursus-ft_nmap.description: Re-coding the nmap command will be the opportunity to deepen your knowledge of TCP/IP networks and thus understand advanced use of threads in real life.
42cursus-ft_nmap.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/215019/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_ping.name: ft_ping
42cursus-ft_ping.description: Re-coding the ping command will allow you to become acquainted with raw IP communication between two machines on a network.
42cursus-ft_ping.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208554/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-ft_traceroute.name: ft_traceroute
42cursus-ft_traceroute.description: Re-coding the traceroute command will be the opportunity to deepen your knowledge of TCP/IP networks by following the paths of an IP packet from one machine to another.
42cursus-ft_traceroute.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/221754/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-gomoku.name: gomoku
42cursus-gomoku.description: This project involves creating, in the language of your choice, a Gomoku game integrating an AI player capable of beating a human player the fastest way possible. To do this, you will implement a min-max algorithm but also do research, trial and error to find the most adapted heuristics. This will not be as easy as checkers.
42cursus-gomoku.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208550/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-3.name: kfs-3
42cursus-kfs-3.description: Third Kernel from Scratch project. Learn how to manage the memory in you kernel.
42cursus-kfs-3.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208611/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-4.name: kfs-4
42cursus-kfs-4.description: Project aimed at creating an Interrupt Description Table and handle interrupts within your Kernel
42cursus-kfs-4.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210779/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-5.name: kfs-5
42cursus-kfs-5.description: You must now develop process managing in your Kernel, by implementing how to interpret the command :(){ :|:& }
42cursus-kfs-5.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210529/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-6.name: kfs-6
42cursus-kfs-6.description: Keep on developping your own kernel. This project will help you set up your own filesystem.
42cursus-kfs-6.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/210527/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-7.name: kfs-7
42cursus-kfs-7.description: This project will teach you how to build your own syscalls for your kernel, as well as user accounts, sockets, and a Unix-like hierarchy. Almost a full kernel here!
42cursus-kfs-7.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/217425/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-8.name: kfs-8
42cursus-kfs-8.description: Build a module interface for your kernel.
42cursus-kfs-8.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208606/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-9.name: kfs-9
42cursus-kfs-9.description: Create an ELF parser and loader for your kernel.
42cursus-kfs-9.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208596/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-kfs-x.name: kfs-x
42cursus-kfs-x.description: This is the final kernel project. It just requires you to create a complete linux environment. Maybe name your kernel aswell?
42cursus-kfs-x.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/208912/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-krpsim.name: krpsim
42cursus-krpsim.description: This algorithm project consists of creating a program that will optimize rendering of a process graph, with some resource constraints. It’s up to you to explore the existing algorithms and choose, possibly create, what you seem most fit. For this project, you can choose the language you want
42cursus-krpsim.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/211241/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-multilayer-perceptron.name: multilayer-perceptron
42cursus-multilayer-perceptron.description: This project is an introduction to artificial neural networks through the implementation of a multilayer perceptron.
42cursus-multilayer-perceptron.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/209575/en.subject.pdf

42cursus-process-and-memory.name: process-and-memory
42cursus-process-and-memory.description: An introduction to syscalls and memory management within linux kernel

In this project you build your own, end to end on your laptop: a local model, a vector index over your code, a retriever that answers grounded questions, and a patch loop that applies, validates, and rolls back when things break. No cloud, no API key, no token bill. By the end, you will know how Copilot and Cursor actually work, because you will have built one.

inception-of-wisdom.name: Inception of wisdom
inception-of-wisdom.description:
Autonomous self-healing on your laptop. The agent watches a real service, notices when it crashes, retrieves the relevant code and config from its own index, asks a local language model what to change, applies the patch, commits it, restarts the service, and rolls everything back when the fix does not take.
 This project ties together what Inception-of-Things taught about GitOps-driven deployment and what Inception-of-Context taught about retrieval-augmented patching, into a closed observe / think / act / verify loop that never leaves the project broken.
 By the end, you will have an agent that catches a bug you planted, finds it without your help, fixes it, and proves it stayed fixed.

datomic.name: Datomic
datomic.description: Datomic is a databases project. On a single self-contained VM you climb twenty levels across six engines (SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, Neo4j and DuckDB), building up SQL and then moving on to columnar, key-value and graph stores. The point is not the syntax of six databases but knowing which tool fits which problem, and federating them instead of duplicating data. Every level draws from a bank of validated variants and your data is renamed for your login, so nobody hands you a solved copy. You discover the SQL yourself in a browser playground and prove it in a live review exam, with nothing to hand in.

ecomesh.name: Ecomesh
ecomesh.description:
One deployment, one year, zero reset. A mesh of battery-powered sensors is dropped in a nature reserve with no way back in: no recharge, no replacement, no repair. Your job is not to build the network, it is to keep it alive and honest.
 You build, in code, a real carbon cost model of the system using the Software Carbon Intensity standard, accounting for both the energy the nodes spend and the carbon embodied in the hardware itself, including what is stranded for good when a node runs out of battery or wears out early. Then you design an adaptive policy that spreads component wear and places computation, so no single node burns out and drags a whole branch of the mesh down with it.
 Everything runs on real Contiki-NG firmware inside a headless Cooja / MSPSim emulation, on a procedurally generated scenario you have never seen and cannot memorize. By the end, you can explain every decision in terms of the Green Software Engineering principles it serves.
ecomesh.subject: https://cdn.intra.42.fr/pdf/pdf/225716/en.subject.pdf
